description_full: KNOT Offshore Partners LP, together with its subsidiaries, acquires, owns, and operates shuttle tankers in the United Kingdom and Brazil. The company loads, transports, condensates, and discharges crude oil from offshore oil field installations to onshore terminals and refineries. It serves oil majors and national oil companies. The company was incorporated in 2013 and is headquartered in Aberdeen, the United Kingdom.

financial_summary: KNOT Offshore Partners LP is a micro-cap energy business with a $296M market cap on $364M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +11% over the past three years and +9% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size.

The business throws off $155M in free cash flow — roughly 43 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 6.70× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 4.2× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin 1.4× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 5.6% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 29% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 2.1× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
